Changelog.title: Updates
Changelog.description: How Ustozona is evolving — new features, improvements, and fixes.

lesson-ai-assistant-launch.title: Lesson editor — AI assistant is live
lesson-ai-assistant-launch.body: The AI assistant in the lesson editor now works: it suggests lesson plans, exercises and quiz questions, takes the current lesson text into account, and its answers can be added to the lesson with one click. Optionally, it can tailor suggestions using anonymous class statistics (average grade, attendance, behavior), or you can upload a textbook/PDF and get answers based only on that document. Each teacher has a daily message limit.

tasks-lesson-duration.title: Tasks — clearer lesson time and focus estimate
tasks-lesson-duration.body: Lesson-based tasks now show both start and end time (e.g. 08:00–08:45). Focus time is now automatically derived from the lesson's actual length — the Planned Time stat reflects it too.

tasks-quick-add-calendar.title: Tasks — mini-calendar and easier quick-add
tasks-quick-add-calendar.body: In the "Today"/"Tomorrow" lists, a weekly mini-calendar lets you jump to any day. The quick-add card now expands with date/flag/class controls in one row. "Today" now shows only tasks due today — overdue ones live in a separate "Overdue" section.

tasks-context-menu.title: Added right-click menu for tasks
tasks-context-menu.body: Right-click a task to quickly change its due date, priority, or class, duplicate it, or mark it as won't do. Pomodoro time selection now uses a wheel picker.

tasks-ui-refresh.title: The Tasks page got easier to use
tasks-ui-refresh.body: The quick-add row is more compact, priority now shows as a flag, and overdue tasks stand out in red. The side panel and detail view also got a refresh.

tasks-hub-launch.title: Tasks — a new automatic task hub
tasks-hub-launch.body: Lessons and assignments now turn into tasks on their own, and you'll get a reminder for each student's birthday. Priority, tags, repeat, and a pomodoro timer — all in one place.

panel-language-v1.title: Panels and cards now look consistent across the whole app
panel-language-v1.body: Classes, Attendance, Gradebook, Tasks and other sections now share one style: the same border, radius, and header height. Sections that used to look slightly different now feel like one product.

toggle-ui-polish.title: View toggles now share one consistent design
toggle-ui-polish.body: All toggles now follow one style: outline border, primary color when selected, background-only hover, and a size that matches the standard button.

tactile-button-depth.title: Primary buttons and segmented toggles now feel pressable
tactile-button-depth.body: Buttons now feel like real buttons with a light-and-shadow effect, and selected segments look pressed in.

student-notes-rebuild.title: Student notes rebuilt: short/full entries, custom tags, and editing
student-notes-rebuild.body: Notes can now have a title, your own tags, search and sorting. You can also edit or delete a note afterwards.

student-profile-tabs-pill-style.title: Student profile section tabs now match the Statistics style

student-profile-bloom-coming-soon.title: Added a "Coming soon" badge to the Bloom's levels card

student-profile-single-edit-mode.title: Student profile: personal info now edits with a single button
student-profile-single-edit-mode.body: Name, gender, birth date, and contact fields now only change when you press "Edit", and only save when you press "Save" — no more accidental changes.

student-breadcrumb-class-crumb.title: Students/profile: the class now shows in the breadcrumb
student-breadcrumb-class-crumb.body: Opening a student from a selected class now shows the class name in the header breadcrumb — click it to quickly jump to another class.

student-preview-card-redesign.title: Student profile: side panel redesigned
student-preview-card-redesign.body: Attendance, grade, and behavior metrics now show together with an icon and percentage. "Metrics" and "Contact" sections are now clearly separated, and the "View Profile" button always stays pinned to the bottom of the panel.

statistics-period-filter-unified.title: Statistics: period filter merged into one menu
statistics-period-filter-unified.body: The Week/Month/Quarter/Year toggle and the period value now live in a single searchable menu. The class table shows student count as a plain number, and the confusing "Signal" column was removed.

statistics-overview-redesign.title: Statistics: Overview tab redesigned
statistics-overview-redesign.body: KPI cards are now in a more logical order: Classes → Students → Attendance → Attention. The student ratio card was updated to show the total in the center; the unhelpful "Averages by gender" card was removed.

bulk-action-floating-bar.title: Bulk actions now appear in a floating bar
bulk-action-floating-bar.body: Selecting multiple rows on the Students or Classes pages now shows a floating bar above the list instead of replacing the toolbar — the header and other buttons stay put.

students-table-view.title: Students: table view and quick actions added
students-table-view.body: You can now view the roster as a table too — click a column to sort, select multiple students to change their status or delete them together. Search and the active filter are now easier to see.

student-attendance-strip-fullyear.title: Student profile: Attendance strip now shows the whole school year
student-attendance-strip-fullyear.body: The strip now spans the full academic year — days that haven't happened yet show as a faded placeholder. Hovering a day now shows just the date.

statistics-class-kpi-expand.title: Statistics: new KPI cards added to the class view
statistics-class-kpi-expand.body: Alongside Active students and Attendance, the class view now also shows Lessons and Assignments counts — a fuller picture of the class at a glance.

statistics-behavior-completion-donuts.title: Statistics: Positive behavior and Completion are now donut charts
statistics-behavior-completion-donuts.body: In the class view, these two indicators are no longer plain percentage cards — Overall behavior (positive/negative, by skill) and Completion (submitted/missing assignments) now render as donut charts next to the gender chart.

statistics-simplified.title: Statistics: the page got simpler
statistics-simplified.body: Grades, Attendance and Behavior are no longer separate tabs — their charts now live right in Overview. With a class selected, every indicator appears in one feed without switching sections.

statistics-class-risk-ranking.title: Statistics: added a ranking of classes needing the most attention
statistics-class-risk-ranking.body: The Overview tab now shows the 3 classes with the most attention signals — tap one to jump to that class. The gender chart now also shows average grade and attendance by gender.

statistics-domain-aggregates.title: Statistics: school-wide charts added to the Grades/Attendance/Behavior tabs
statistics-domain-aggregates.body: With no class selected, these tabs now show a weekly attendance trend, grade distribution, behavior climate, and a class ranking. List rows are now fully clickable — extra buttons were removed.

statistics-risk-view.title: Statistics: the “Needs attention” section is now student-centric
statistics-risk-view.body: At-risk students now show in a single list ranked by risk level — no student is scattered across several cards. The attendance KPI now shows the trend vs. the previous period.

statistics-students-tab.title: Added a “Students” tab to the Statistics page
statistics-students-tab.body: You can now see every student across all your classes in one table: sort by attendance, grade, trend, and risk level.

classes-page-rename.title: The “My classes” section is now called “Classes” for short

changelog-link-labels-fix.title: Fixed link labels on the Updates page

classes-table-view.title: Table view added to the Classes page
classes-table-view.body: You can now view your classes as Cards, a List, or a compact Table. In Table view, you can select multiple classes and archive or delete them all at once.

statistics-table-polish.title: Minor fixes in the Statistics table
statistics-table-polish.body: The attendance percentage used to show as a long decimal — it's now always rounded. The unnecessary line under the header and the unused selection/action columns were removed.

tasks-calendar-launch.title: Calendar view on the Tasks page
tasks-calendar-launch.body: The Tasks page now has a calendar alongside the list: lessons, task deadlines, holidays, and birthdays for the day, week, month, quarter, and year all show in one place. Click any entry to jump straight to it.

statistics-launch.title: New section: Statistics
statistics-launch.body: See the full picture across all your classes in one place: who needs attention, which class needs more of your time, grade distribution, standards mastery, and attendance and behavior trends. Open a class for assignment difficulty and class-level detail.

home-redesign-command-center.title: The home page is now your command center for the day
home-redesign-command-center.body: Your day is now visible at a glance: “Up next” gathers tasks, ungraded work, and deadlines into one list; “Needs attention” surfaces students with dropping attendance or falling grades on its own; today's lessons appear on the right as a list or a timeline. Upcoming birthdays are here too, and quotes you control appear at the end of the day.

multi-language-support.title: The app now works in 6 languages
multi-language-support.body: Choose your language from Settings — Uzbek, Karakalpak, Kyrgyz, Kazakh, Russian, or English. The whole app (menus, buttons, pages) switches to that language.

student-profile-class-badge-fix.title: Fixed the class badge on the student profile
student-profile-class-badge-fix.body: The class color badge was too small and looked like a circle — it's now the same rounded-square shape everywhere. The class used to appear twice, under the name and in “Personal info” — now it shows only once.

student-auto-id.title: Every student now gets an automatic ID
student-auto-id.body: When you add a new student, they're now automatically assigned a sequential ID — no need to enter one by hand.

card-passport-v2.title: Cards and lists have a new look
card-passport-v2.body: Classes, lessons, students, and timetable cards all share a new, consistent look: rounded gradient icons, a thin colored line on the left when selected. Extra info on student cards (the ID row) was removed, so key metrics stand out more clearly.

class-color-palette-expanded.title: Class color palette expanded
class-color-palette-expanded.body: When you create a new class, a color is now assigned automatically — no color repeats until every color has been used. 7 new shades (yellow, lime, emerald, teal, violet, fuchsia, rose) were added to the color picker — choose from 17 colors in total.

guided-tour-reliability.title: Guided tours are now more reliable
guided-tour-reliability.body: A tour is no longer wrongly marked “seen” if you're on a small screen or navigate away mid-tour. A skipped tour no longer gets confused with a completed one, and you can now navigate with the keyboard (Esc, arrow keys).

profile-birthdate-save-fix.title: Saving a birth date in your profile now works
profile-birthdate-save-fix.body: In Settings > Profile, picking a birth date via year/day/month sometimes left the “Save” button inactive — fixed.

students-add-flow.title: Adding students now works
students-add-flow.body: A “No class selected” error was blocking students from being added in some cases — fixed. The add-student dialog was also redesigned: adding one student, pasting a list, or importing from a CSV/Excel file now all happen in one convenient dialog. (Thanks to Omadbek Odilov for finding these bugs in testing!)

lesson-editor-save-fix.title: Saving in the lesson editor is now reliable
lesson-editor-save-fix.body: Text you wrote in the lesson editor could previously disappear — going back to the lessons list made it look like your changes weren't saved. Every change is now saved to the server immediately, so nothing is lost when you leave the page.

notifications-polish.title: Notifications are more convenient
notifications-polish.body: When your feedback's status changes, the exact stage (e.g. under review) now shows immediately with a colored badge. Clicking a notification now takes you straight to the right feedback card.

changelog-launch.title: The Updates page is live
changelog-launch.body: You can now track what's changing in Ustozona right from this page. A badge appears in the sidebar whenever something new ships.

feedback-v2.title: Feedback got stronger
feedback-v2.body: You get a notification when the team replies to your feedback or its status changes — one click takes you straight to it.

prod-launch.title: Ustozona is now live on the internet: www.ustozona.uz
prod-launch.body: The platform launched at its official address. Sign in to your account with one click via Google.

command-palette.title: Quick search — Ctrl+K
command-palette.body: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) to instantly find any page, class, or student. The bar at the top of the page also lets you switch quickly between classes and students.

student-profile-real.title: The student profile is now fully functional
student-profile-real.body: Notes on the profile are now saved for good, and the attendance section shows real attendance results.

motion-polish.title: The interface came to life
motion-polish.body: Pages open with smooth animation, and cards give a responsive feel when clicked — everything feels more pleasant to use.

multi-year.title: Work across multiple academic years
multi-year.body: Moving to a new academic year is now easier: archive last year's classes and start the new one with a clean gradebook. Past years' data isn't lost — you can revisit it anytime.

behavior-auto-points.title: Behavior points are now also added automatically
behavior-auto-points.body: Based on attendance and gradebook results, automatic additions are now made to a student's behavior score — no need to enter them by hand.

settings-redesign.title: Settings was reorganized
settings-redesign.body: Sections are now grouped by topic, and changes are confirmed with a clear “Save” button — you always see exactly what you've changed.

behavior-launch.title: Behavior page
behavior-launch.body: Award points to students for skills, give out rewards, and see a class-wide behavior report — all on one page.

page-tours.title: Guided walkthroughs on every page
page-tours.body: The Planner, Gradebook, Attendance, and other pages now have step-by-step walkthroughs — open one anytime from the cap icon at the top.

guidehub.title: Guide hub: open a walkthrough whenever you need it

onboarding-v2.title: The setup wizard has a new look

bell-settings.title: Bell schedule and academic year settings
bell-settings.body: View the bell schedule as a calendar, and manage the academic year's quarters and breaks on a timeline.

home-redesign.title: The home page has a new look
home-redesign.body: Today's lessons, a weekly calendar, and a greeting card — plan your day at a glance.

onboarding-launch.title: A ready-made start for new users
onboarding-launch.body: When you sign up, you add your classes, and the calendar is automatically set up to match the academic year.

account-delete-fix.title: Fixed an account deletion bug
account-delete-fix.body: Deleted data used to reappear when signing back in even after deleting your account — deletion now works completely.

nav-simpler.title: Navigation simplified: a cleaner sidebar and header

backend-v1.title: Real accounts and cloud storage
backend-v1.body: Your data is no longer stored in the browser — it's now kept securely on a server. Sign in from any device and your classes and gradebook are right there.

timetable-uz.title: The timetable is now in Uzbek and uses 24-hour format

classes-polish.title: The home page and classes were polished

standards-launch.title: Standards page
standards-launch.body: Track education standards by Bloom's taxonomy levels.

initial-release.title: Ustozona launched
initial-release.body: First version: classes, attendance, and timetable — all built to make a teacher's daily work easier.

tasks-stats-panel.title: Tasks — stats panel added on the right
tasks-stats-panel.body: When no task is selected, the right panel now shows planned time, planned tasks, time spent, and completion rate at a glance, plus a shortcut to full statistics.

0.title: Get to know your workspace
0.body: Every page — schedule, lessons, grades, attendance — lives in this sidebar. Need more room? Collapse it with the button above.

1.title: Your day's command center
1.body: The greeting chips are clickable: checks lead to the gradebook, the attendance counter to the attendance page. The thin bar below tracks the school year — hover the season marks to see quarter dates.

2.title: Work queue
2.body: Tasks, ungraded work, and upcoming assessments share one queue. Use “Today” in the header to widen the horizon (week or all), and “+ Task” adds one right here.

3.title: Today's lessons
3.body: Switch between list and timeline — your choice is remembered. Past lessons fade, the current one stands out; after the last lesson a day-summary card appears where you can manage your own quotes.

4.title: Week strip
4.body: Picking a day changes only the lessons panel — the work queue keeps looking at today. A dot under a day means a lesson is planned.

5.title: Guide hub
5.body: Forgot how a section works? Click this button — you can replay any page's guide at any time.

6.title: Your feedback matters
6.body: Found a bug or have a suggestion? Send it straight to the team from here — you can attach a screenshot too.

0.title: It all starts here
0.body: First create a new class: enter its name, subject, and a distinguishing color. Every other section (schedule, students, gradebook, attendance) links back to these classes.

1.title: Class card
1.body: Each card shows the number of students, topics, and assignments at a glance. Click a card to open the full class page.

2.title: Switch the view
2.body: You can view your classes as a grid or a list — pick whichever view suits you best.

3.title: Overall stats
3.body: This section totals up all classes, students, lessons, and assignments. These numbers update automatically as you add new classes.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick a class on the left to see its students. Each class shows how many students it has.

1.title: Student list
1.body: See every student in the class at once. Click a card to open their profile on the right. Click the status badge to switch between active/on leave (right-click to archive).

2.title: Student details
2.body: Review the student's class, contact details, and quick actions without leaving the page. Click “View profile” for full attendance, grades, notes, and their personal portfolio.

3.title: Filter by status
3.body: Sort students by status (active, on leave, archived) — handy for focusing on the students who need attention.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Create your classes here first. Each gets its own color so you can tell them apart easily on the calendar.

1.title: Weekly schedule
1.body: Your recurring lesson schedule is stored here. If your schedule alternates week to week, set up a rotation cycle — the calendar will then mark each day automatically.

2.title: Drag from the side panel
2.body: Grab a class card from the side panel and drag it onto an empty calendar slot. This works in every view.

3.title: Or click a cell
3.body: In “Schedule” view you can also click an empty cell and pick the class from the list. Great for placing lessons quickly and precisely.

0.title: Empty lesson slots
0.body: Each block is a scheduled lesson slot. Hover over it: use the “+” button to create a new lesson, or the link icon to attach an existing one.

1.title: Linked lessons
1.body: Once a lesson is attached, the block fills with color and shows the lesson name. Click it to edit, or drag it to another slot.

2.title: Day settings
2.body: Hover over a day to reveal this button — from here you can block the day or jump to editing the schedule.

3.title: Month view
3.body: Switch to Month view to see the whole schedule at a glance. Colored lines mark scheduled classes, and document icons mark days with linked lessons.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick a class to view its lessons and units. Each shows how many units and lessons it has.

1.title: Organize into units
1.body: Units help split your lessons into chapters or topics. Create units to organize your curriculum — drag them to reorder.

2.title: Your lessons
2.body: Create individual lessons inside each unit. Every lesson card shows its status and date.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick any class to see its attendance table. You can mark the whole class's daily attendance here.

1.title: Attendance table
1.body: The table is organized by student and date. Click the relevant cell to mark a student's attendance (present, absent, late, or excused). Changes save instantly.

2.title: Configure statuses
2.body: This button opens Settings > Attendance. From there you can turn attendance statuses on or off and set how much each one affects the overall attendance rate.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick a class to award points. Just like attendance and the gradebook, one class stays open at a time here.

1.title: Award points
1.body: Click a student's card to award them points individually, or use the “Whole class” card to award everyone at once.

2.title: Award several at once
2.body: Hover over a card and a circle appears in the corner — use it to select multiple students and award them points in one go.

3.title: Class report
3.body: See the positive/negative point distribution for the whole class or a single student over a period, right here.

4.title: Points history
4.body: A full chronological list of every point awarded — delete an entry or add a note from here whenever needed.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick a class to open its gradebook. Each class shows how many students are enrolled and how many assignments have been created.

1.title: Grading topics
1.body: Topics group your assignments and set their share of the final grade. Set weights that add up to 100%, then click a topic to filter the table.

2.title: Your gradebook
2.body: Every student and assignment appears in a table view. Click any cell to enter or edit a grade. The overall result updates automatically based on topic weights.

0.title: Your classes
0.body: Pick any class to see its standards list. Each class has its own set of standards.

1.title: Add curriculum standards
1.body: You can add standards from national and regional education frameworks. Filter by country, region, subject, and grade level to find the right set for your class.

2.title: Track coverage
2.body: Each standard shows its mastery status — green means a lesson is linked, gray means none yet. You link standards from the lesson editor, and linked lessons show up here automatically.

0.title: Tasks panel
0.body: Get a quick overview of your tasks in the left panel. It has smart lists (Today, Important, Overdue…), sorting by class, and ready-made templates (create a task in one click).

1.title: Organize your work
1.body: Grading, planning lessons, or communicating with parents — create a task for anything you want to track. Group them with colored tags and sort by status, priority, or tag.

2.title: Quick add
2.body: Type right in the task input: attach a date, priority, and class using the toolbar buttons.

3.title: Stats panel
3.body: The right panel shows change trends and workload for the selected time range.

0.title: Write your feedback
0.body: Send Ustozona a suggestion, bug report, question, or compliment right here — pick a category and attach a screenshot if needed.

1.title: All, In progress, Done
1.body: Track every submission and its current status across the tabs. Search and sorting tools are on the right.

2.title: Why voting matters
2.body: Click ↑ on a suggestion you like — suggestions with more votes are prioritized by the team and shipped sooner. That's the suggestions' “priority ranking”.
